exposure: Early onset of preeclampsia (<34 weeks gestation)
cohort: 482 preeclamptic patients who delivered in the Southern part of Reunion Island between January 1, 2015 and January 1, 2019
finding: Women with preeclampsia requiring ICU admission had a higher risk of HELLP syndrome, severe post-partum hemorrhage, and early onset preeclampsia, leading to higher rates of C-section and poorer fetal outcomes, but there were no maternal deaths.
mod_finding: C-section rate was higher in the ICU group compared to controls (OR 2.83 [1.67-4.78], p<.001).
gest_age: Early onset of preeclampsia defined as <34 weeks gestation
birth_weight: Lower birth weight in infants of mothers admitted to ICU (1776g vs. 2304g, p<.001)
